I or T: B1 [ I or T ] to fasten together two ends of a piece of string or other long, thin material, or to (cause to) hold together with a long, thin piece of string, material, etc.

often passive: › [ often passive ] to force someone to stay in a place

T: › [ T ] to relate to or connect to

I: › [ I ] to finish at the same time or score the same number of points, etc. in a competition as someone or something else

C: A2 US also necktie a long, thin piece of material that is worn under a shirt collar, especially by men, and tied in a knot at the front
› any piece of string, plastic, metal, etc. that is used to fasten or hold together something
› the friendly feelings that people have for other people, or special connections with places
C2 a situation in which two or more people finish at the same time or score the same number of points

example: Could you tie this piece of string for me?
你能幫我把這個繩子打個結嗎？
This skirt ties at the waist.
這條連衣裙是在腰間繫帶的。
She tied the ribbon tightly in a bow/knot.
她把絲帶打成一個緊緊的蝴蝶結。
I tie my hair back when it's hot.
天熱時我就把頭髮繫在腦後。
Tie (up) your shoelaces, or you'll trip over them.
把鞋帶繫好，不然會摔跤的。
I felt tied to the job while I had a mortgage to pay.
因為有按揭貸款要還，我覺得自己被這份工作束縛住了。
Her job ties her to the east coast.
她的工作把她約束在東海岸。
Is the allergy tied to dairy products, for example?
比如說，過敏症與奶製品有關係嗎？
Can you tie his behaviour up with anything that's happened recently?
你認為他的行為與最近發生的甚麼事有關聯嗎？
The Republicans are trying to tie the funding up with this bill.
共和黨試圖把資金與這項法案聯繫起來。
Jane and I tied (for first place) in the spelling test.
在拼寫比賽中（爭奪第一名時）我和簡打成平手。
We tied with a team from the south in the championships.
在錦標賽中我們和一支南方隊打成平手。
He always wears a jacket and tie to work.
他上班時總是穿西服打領帶。
Can you see the ties for the rubbish bags in the cupboard?
你看到櫃子裡綁垃圾袋的帶子嗎？
Family ties are weaker if you move a long way away.
離家太遠就會與家人疏遠。
I no longer feel any ties with my home town.
我對我的家鄉再也沒有任何親切感了。
He urged governments worldwide to break diplomatic ties with the new regime.
他敦促世界各國政府斷絕與新政權的外交關係。
It's a tie for first place.
兩人並列第一。
They have changed the scoring system because there have been too many ties.
因為常常出現不分勝負的結果，他們改變了計分制。

NONE: › to hold someone or something in place with ropes
（用繩子）捆住，栓住

example: Tie down anything that might blow away in the storm.
把有可能被風暴吹走的所有東西全部拴住。

NONE: › When ideas or statements tie in, they agree or are closely connected, and if you tie them in, you make them agree or connect closely.
（使）相一致；（使）有聯繫

example: I can't tie in what he said today with what he told me last week.
他今天說的與上週他告訴我的根本就不是一回事。

NONE: › to plan an event or activity so that it combines with or happens at the same time as another, or to be planned in this way
（使）同時發生

example: We're trying to tie our holiday in with Jaimie's business trip.
我們試圖把我們的假期與傑米的出差行程安排在一起。

NONE: › to confuse someone
使（某人）困惑，把（某人）弄糊塗

example: The Director of Studies tied me up in knots by asking tricky questions.
教務主任問了一些很難回答的問題，把我弄得頭昏腦脹。

M often passive: › [ M often passive ] to limit someone's freedom

NONE: › to make someone give you a clear decision
使（某人）明確表態

example: He's tied down by having to work every Saturday.
他星期六都被工作綁住了。
We'd like to travel more, but having children at school really ties us down.
我們想去更多的地方旅遊，可是孩子要上學，把我們綁住了。
I'll try to tie her down on her plans.
我會設法讓她把計劃確定下來。

NONE: B2 to make a person unable to move by tying a rope or something similar around their body or part of their body
把（某人）捆綁起來
› When someone is tied up, they are busy or prevented from doing something, such as speaking to someone or going somewhere, because of being involved in another event or activity.
把（某人）纏住，使（某人）無法脫身

example: The burglars had tied him up (to the bed).
竊賊們把他捆了起來（綁在床上）。
I'm afraid we can't meet till Wednesday - I'm tied up on Monday and Tuesday.
恐怕我們要到週三才能碰頭——我週一和週二都脫不開身。
Mrs Moran is tied up in a meeting at the moment, but I'll ask her to call you later.
莫蘭夫人現在正開會脫不開身，我會告訴她稍後給你打電話。

NONE: › to fasten something together using string, rope, or something similar
（用繩子、線等）捆紮
› to cause something, often money or possessions, not to be available for use
佔用（常指資金、產業等）

example: It was an old-fashioned parcel, tied up with string.
這是一個老式的包裹，用細線綁著。
All my money is tied up in property.
我所有的資金都投在房地產上，無法動用。
He tied up the printer all morning, printing out copies of his presentation.
他整個早上一直佔著印表機列印他的報告。

NONE: C2 to get married
結婚

example: So when are you two going to tie the knot?
那麼你倆甚麼時候結婚呢？

NONE: › extra play at the end of a game when both teams have the same points, to decide who is the winner
（當兩隊在比賽結束時打成平局而增加的）決勝局，加時賽
› to colour cloth by tying it in knots so that when it is put in a dye (= substance for changing the colour of cloth) the tied areas absorb less colour and produce circular patterns when unfastened
紮染

example: There are pictures of my grandparents in the 60s wearing flares and tie-dyed T-shirts.
有幾張60年代我的祖父母穿著喇叭褲和紮染T恤衫的照片。

NONE: › a product such as a toy or book that is related to a film, television programme, etc.
相關產品（與某一電影、電視節目等有關的產品，如玩具或書籍）

C: › mainly UK a connection or agreement that joins two things or organizations
› US a temporary problem that delays progress, such as too much traffic on the road

example: Cambridge University Press arranged a tie-up with the German publisher Klett.
劍橋大學出版社籌劃了與德國克勒特出版社的一次合作。
I missed my flight because of a tie-up on the interstate.
由於州際公路上交通堵塞，我錯過了航班。

NONE: › a house owned by your employer that you can live in for as long as you are employed in a particular job
（僱主在僱員受僱期間租給其居住的）僱工農舍
› a pub that is owned by a particular beer company and only sells that company's products
（啤酒廠開設的）專賣酒店

example: Compare
free house

NONE: › If you say that someone, especially a man, is tied to his mother's/wife's apron strings, it means that he is strongly influenced and controlled by that person.
受母親／老婆的管束
› a small, thin, often decorative piece of metal used to hold the two parts of a tie together
領帶扣針，領帶別針
› one of several layers or levels
（多層、多層次中的）一層
› to arrange or organize something in tiers
層疊；層層排列

example: We sat in one of the upper tiers of the football stands.
我們坐在足球場看臺的上層位置。
My wedding cake had four tiers, each supported by small pillars.
我的結婚蛋糕有四層，每層都由小柱子撐著。
I don't understand why you think we need yet another tier of management.
我不明白你為甚麼認為我們還需要一個管理層級。
The seats in the theatre were steeply tiered.
劇院的座位呈陡直的階梯狀排列。
